draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Gangaikonda Cholapuram! This quiet village was the capital of the Chola Empire for about 250 years, founded by Rajendra I around 1025. Its name means 'the city of the Chola who took the Ganges', and his great Shiva temple is just a minute's walk away.
draft.hungryLine: There's nowhere much to eat in this sleepy village, so have a proper meal before you come and bring water and snacks.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Brihadisvara Temple is a 1 min walk from here, and the Viranarayanan Perumal Temple is about 20 minutes away on foot.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a shady corner in the temple complex and take in the huge tower and the famous Nandi.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Rajendra I brought water all the way from the Ganges to set up his new capital, and that's where the village gets its name.

spots.name: Brihadisvara Temple
spots.detail: 1 min walk · Rajendra Chola I's temple, finished in 1035 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site

spots.name: Viranarayanan perumal temple
spots.detail: 20 min walk · A Perumal temple in the same village

legends.title: Water from the Ganges
legends.body: Locals tell how Rajendra I sent an expedition to bring water from the Ganges to establish his new capital. The village's name, the city of the Chola who took the Ganges, still remembers it.

tips.title: Come at sunrise.
tips.body: The temple opens to the sunrise, with its sanctum and halls lined up on an east to west axis.

tips.title: Bring your own supplies.
tips.body: Apart from the temple, the old capital is a desolate place, so carry water and snacks.

story.title: A victory capital
story.body: Rajendra I founded the city to celebrate his win over the Pala dynasty and made it the Chola capital. He named it for his expedition to the Ganges.

story.title: The great temple
story.body: Rajendra Chola I completed the Brihadisvara Temple here. It's similar in design and name to the older Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur, about 70 km away, smaller but more refined.

story.title: Seat of an empire
story.body: Gangaikonda Cholapuram stayed the Chola capital for around 250 years. The temple's walls are still covered in sculpture, artwork and inscriptions from that time.

story.title: Only the temple remains
story.body: The rest of the capital and its other Chola temples were completely destroyed, leaving a small village. The surviving temple is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
